blocks.text: The map() method creates a new array with the results of calling a function for every array element.

const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4];
const doubled = numbers.map(x => x * 2);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The map() method is commonly used in React to render lists of elements:

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: When using map() in React to create list items, each item needs a unique key prop.
You can also use map() with arrays of objects:

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The map() method takes three parameters:

items: currentValue - The current element being processed
index - The index of the current element (optional)
array - The array that map was called upon (optional)

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: The map() method always returns a new array. It does not modify the original array.
